<!-- Sandbox (path.yml form: sandbox). Guide: assets/learn/README.md, "Sandboxes and
     capstones". Replace <slug> with the sandbox's JS name and <id> with its path.yml id.
     Order: the brief (the site or system, what the reader decides, what the engine works out, what it leaves out, and
     presets to start from) -> the bench (controls; Run; the run's status; the plan link) -> the results (readouts, the
     hourly year or the outage scenarios, a text version) -> explain (how the engine works; where it holds: LX.Boundary)
     -> sources. The step links are #brief, #bench, #results, #explain and #sources (the build checks that each exists);
     the screenshot tool reaches each one as sec-brief, sec-bench, sec-results and sec-sources, and `explain` shows
     #explain.
     The engine (E0 for SB0, E1 for SB1, ...) is a shared component, written in
     assets/learn/components/<engine>.js, so the capstones (and A8, M5) run the same model. The page expects:
       engine.schema                      the plan as an LX.ShareState schema (fields, ranges, steps, defaults, version,
                                          older versions with up()); one source for the controls, the link and the tests
       engine.presets                     [{ id, label, state }] the brief's starting plans (each passes the schema)
       engine.solve(state, data, { signal, timeLimit, attempt }) -> Promise of
         { status, ok, message, hint, results, kind, mipGap, ms }   never rejects; status as LX.solver's (optimal,
                                          infeasible, time-limit, objective-bound, error, cancelled, ...); ok only when
                                          the status is optimal; `hint` says what to change after an infeasible plan
                                          ("raise the battery or shed the offices"); `results` only when a plan exists
       engine.summarize(state, r) -> results   pure: every number the page shows (readouts, chart series, text tables),
                                          tested against the page and the no-JS block
       engine.note(state, results) -> the LX.ReportNote input (heading, made, run, plan, results, assumptions,
                                          sensitivity, limits); the capstone adds its own fields
       engine.fallback(data) -> HTML      the default plan's inputs and results as plain tables (a precomputed run, with
                                          its date), for the no-JS blocks below
     Failure states: run through LX.BenchRun. It shows a clear message and "Try again" after a
     failure, a time limit or an infeasible plan, clears the busy state, keeps the results already drawn (marked as an
     earlier plan's) and passes `attempt` so a retry can raise the time limit. Test it with a stubbed solve that fails.
     Ties: an LP or MILP with several optima of equal cost makes "the" dispatch arbitrary: state the tie rule
     in the engine (a tiny cost on battery throughput, a fixed order) or show only what every optimum shares; prove it in
     the test. No false certificates: "optimal" only for status optimal; a MILP shows its gap; an early stop
     never says best. A "jump", "always" or "never" in the text must hold in the model as built, shown by the test.
     State: controls continue from the reader's plan (presets fill the controls; they never reset hidden
     parts), focus survives a re-render, results are announced (BenchRun's status line), and a busy run holds Next.
     The plan link (LX.ShareState): numbers and choices only, no free text and no personal data; the schema's version
     goes up whenever a field, a range, a step or a meaning changes, with an `old` entry so earlier links still open.
     Prices in one dollar year, labeled; data scaled or invented is "illustrative" or "based on ...", never "real".
     Scope (the course's scope rules): Prairie Town, Prairie Campus and their sites are fictional; data centers appear
     only as loads; no links to project pages or the Research page; the course author's research only through approved
     excerpts, allow-listed repositories and citations (the sourcing rule).
     After editing path.yml, run the course build step (it fills the three marker blocks below; never edit them by
     hand). -->

<div><dt>The engine works out</dt><dd>One line: what the model chooses or runs (an hourly year, outage scenarios), and its goal.</dd></div>

::: {#bench .lx-sec}
::: {.lx-sec-h}
## The bench
:::

```{=html}
<!-- The live bench: div.lx-sb with div.lx-sb-controls (a fieldset.lx-sb-group per group of controls: LX.Slider,
     LX.Toggle, a div.lx-seg of buttons with aria-pressed) and div.lx-sb-side (the presets, LX.BenchRun, the readouts,
     LX.ShareState). Build the controls from engine.schema, start them from ShareState's `state` (a link's plan, or the
     defaults), and on every change call ss.set(plan) and run.changed(plan). Readouts beside the controls go in
     BenchRun's `results` too, so they dim with the results when the plan changes. The fallback is complete: the
     default plan and what each control can do. -->
<div class="lx-interactive" data-learn="<slug>" data-src="../assets/learn/data/<id>.json ../assets/learn/data/path.json">
<div class="lx-fallback lx-sb-static">
<!-- <slug>-bench:start (written from engine.schema by LX.ShareState.staticHTML in the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<table class="lx-facts"><thead><tr><th scope="col">Control</th><th scope="col">Default plan</th><th scope="col">Range</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>Solar PV</td><td class="n">6 kW</td><td>0 to 20 kW, in steps of 0.5 kW</td></tr></tbody></table>
<!-- <slug>-bench:end -->
<p class="lx-hint">With JavaScript on, you change these, run the year in your browser, and copy a link to your plan.</p>
</div>
</div>
<p class="lx-datanote"><span>Where the inputs come from, with dates (or: the site and its loads are illustrative, based on ...). Prices in 20XX dollars.</span></p>
```
:::
